subject.title: fix: stabilize embedded prompt caching across policy and Responses boundaries

question: Is it acceptable for non-owner and ambient turns to see protected `computer`, `cron`, `gateway`, and `nodes` schemas when every execution path is denied by an immutable current-turn grant before hooks or side effects?
rationale: Source review can verify enforcement mechanics, but only maintainers can define whether protected schema visibility itself is an accepted security and product boundary.

options.title: Accept visible schemas
options.body: Approve stable schema visibility provided exact-head proof demonstrates denial before hooks and side effects in both in-process and MCP paths.

options.title: Keep schemas hidden
options.body: Preserve inventory filtering for unauthorized turns and accept the resulting prompt-cache churn.

options.title: Reduce exposed metadata
options.body: Use stable placeholder schemas or reduced descriptions if full protected tool metadata is considered sensitive.

recommendation.title: Accept visible schemas
recommendation.body: Approve stable schema visibility provided exact-head proof demonstrates denial before hooks and side effects in both in-process and MCP paths.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Codex lifecycle and binding work is the strongest available individual routing signal, though security ownership is shared.
